requirement:
Rust reports line and block comments, including outer and inner documentation
comments, as `Comment`. An outer attribute (`#[…]`) attached to an outline
item is an `Annotation` on that item. These are the two kinds Rust reports.
For example, a function preceded by `/// Verify the token.` and `#[inline]`
owns a `Comment` followed by an `Annotation`. A file-level `//!` comment
belongs to the file root.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.attachments`. I judged this from the supplied test source only and did not read the implementation.

Obligations and the tests that cover them:
- **Line comments are `Comment`, including outer and inner doc comments.** `rust_attachments_keep_the_owner_kind_and_original_bytes` uses a file with `//! file docs`, two `/// café` lines and a trailing `// trailing`. It asserts that each is a `Comment`, and that its span text matches the original source bytes.
- **Block comments are `Comment`, including outer and inner doc forms.** The `blocks.rs` case in `bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax` covers `/*! inner */`, `/** outer */` and `/* ordinary */`. It asserts that all three are `Comment`.
- **An outer attribute on an outline item is an `Annotation` on that item.** The first test attaches `#[inline]` to `fn f` and asserts `(Annotation, "#[inline]")` in the attachments of the `mod[m]/fn[f]` item (`items[2]`).
- **The function example: `/// …` plus `#[inline]` gives a `Comment` followed by an `Annotation`.** The first test asserts the exact ordered list for `fn f`: `Comment`, `Comment`, `Annotation`, then the trailing `Comment`. It also asserts that the spans do not overlap.
- **A file-level `//!` comment belongs to the file root.** The first test asserts that the root item (`items[0]`) holds `(Comment, "//! file docs")`. It also asserts that the `mod m` item has no attachments, so the comment is not misattributed.
- **Only these two kinds are reported.** The assertions compare exact kind and text lists, so an extra or different kind would fail them.

I found no gap. The text does not specify inner attributes (`#![…]`) or attributes on non-outline constructs, so I did not require tests for them. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.
